country.comment: Study examines post-earthquake internally displaced person (IDP) camps in the Port-au-Prince metropolitan area of Haiti.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title, Abstract, and Introduction; PDF p. 3, Methodology (Sampling)

effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative bivariate/three-way contingency table results from the 99-camp survey paired with January 2011 follow-up and qualitative findings on land ownership and state-NGO coordination.
effect_estimate.value: Seven months post-earthquake (July–August 2010), 42.3% (30/71) of surveyed IDP camps had no water provided and 29.2% (26/89) had no toilets (averaging 273 people per toilet; 32.0% [16/50] cleaned every 3+ days vs. 68.0% [34/50] every 1–2 days), with minimal overall improvement by January 2011 (38.6% [32/83] without water; 25.5% [24/94] without toilets). NGO-managed camps were significantly more likely than non-NGO-managed camps to have water provided (88.5% [23/26] vs. 40.0% [18/45]; chi-square(1, N=71) = 15.86, p = 0.000) and toilets present (90.3% [28/31] vs. 59.6% [34/57]; chi-square(1, N=88) = 9.08, p = 0.002), whereas toilet cleaning frequency did not differ significantly (73.9% [17/23] vs. 63.0% [17/27]). Camp location was significantly associated with water provision (73.9% [34/46] central vs. 50.0% [1/2] Cité Soleil vs. 26.1% [6/23] peripheral; chi-square(2, N=71) = 14.43, p = 0.001) and toilet presence (81.8% [45/55] central vs. 71.4% [5/7] Cité Soleil vs. 46.2% [12/26] peripheral; chi-square(2, N=88) = 10.79, p = 0.005), though peripheral camps with NGO management had 100% water (2/2 vs. 19.0% [4/21]) and 100% toilets (4/4 vs. 36.4% [8/22]). Public vs. private land ownership showed higher but non-significant differences for water (75.0% [9/12] vs. 51.8% [29/56]) and toilets (75.0% [15/20] vs. 67.7% [44/65])—while significantly affecting on-site clinics (39.1% [9/23] vs. 12.9% [9/70]; chi-square(1, N=93) = 7.66, p = 0.009)—with qualitative evidence documenting private landowners blocking NGOs and cutting off water/aid to force IDPs to leave, whereas DINEPA-led coordination with local government and NGOs raised Cité Soleil camp water coverage to 100% and reduced camps without toilets to 14.3% (1/7) by January 2011.

mechanism_certainty.comment: Mixed-methods design (MMAT ceiling of 2). Direct camp observations and 57 semi-structured interviews directly document private landowners blocking NGO WASH delivery to evict IDPs, voluntary NGOs avoiding underserved camps and camp-manager registration due to perceived legal liability and fragmented accountability, formal red-zone travel restrictions, and state-led DINEPA coordination achieving full camp water coverage in Cité Soleil.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines public vs. private land ownership/tenure conflicts where private owners blocked or cut off WASH services to evict IDPs, municipal/red-zone geographical service boundaries, voluntary NGO discretion in selecting camps and avoiding legal liability, institutional fragmentation across NGOs/clusters/weakened state agencies, state-led DINEPA political/inter-agency coordination in Cité Soleil, November 2011 government termination of water trucking, and exclusion/inclusion of local actors in cluster coordination.
